0.0.n: This company designation comes before the name Venture House in Japanese.

0.1.n: This is the first part of the company name Venture House.

0.3.n: This is the second part of the company name Venture House.

0.4.n: Links the company to the speaker, showing his affiliation.

0.5.n: This is the speaker’s family name, placed before his given name.

0.6.n: 恵人 is the speaker’s given name; its reading is supplied by the translation.

0.7.n: Marks the name being stated before 申します.

0.8.n: The polite form of humble 申す, used to introduce yourself respectfully.

0.10.n: Combines with お願いします to make a conventional greeting after an introduction.

0.11.n: A polite request that completes よろしくお願いします, a standard expression when meeting someone.

1.0.n: Sets the time frame for the company’s present work.

1.2.n: Combines with 代行 to describe performing sales work for other businesses.

1.3.n: Follows 営業 to name the business of handling sales for clients.

1.4.n: Introduces the label 営業代行 before の turns it into something the speaker can discuss.

1.5.n: Stands for the activity just named and allows it to become the object of やる.

1.6.n: Marks 営業代行というの as what the company does.

1.7.n: An English loanword followed by で to describe the company’s primary activity.

1.8.n: With メイン, indicates that this work is the company’s main activity.

1.9.n: やる becomes やって, followed by おります, a humble, polite alternative to います.

2.0.n: 扱う becomes 扱っている, describing the products the company currently deals with.

2.1.n: A business term for goods or services offered to customers.

2.2.n: Combines with は to introduce the perspective of products handled.

2.3.n: Marks the products handled as the topic of the explanation.

2.5.n: Names one service category the company sells.

2.6.n: Lists examples without suggesting that these are the only categories.

2.7.n: 系 adds the sense of a category or field to 電気.

2.8.n: Links the service categories to 事業.

2.9.n: Here, the speaker loosely uses this for the service offerings being sold.

2.10.n: Introduces the preceding description before の packages it as the thing being sold.

2.11.n: Stands for the previously described business offerings so they can be marked with を.

2.12.n: Marks the described offerings as what the company sells.

2.13.n: Combines with 販売 to form 訪問販売, meaning door-to-door sales.

2.14.n: Together with 訪問, names the method of selling through visits to customers.

2.15.n: Follows 訪問販売 to indicate that door-to-door selling is the primary method.

2.16.n: In 中心に, shows what the selling activity centers on.

2.17.n: 販売する becomes 販売させていただいています, a deferential expression literally presenting the activity as something one is allowed to do.

3.0.n: 僕 plus ら refers to the speaker and his group; it sounds less formal than 私たち.

3.1.n: Links 僕ら to 会社 to show whose company it is.

3.2.n: Refers to the business the speaker represents.

3.3.n: Links 会社 to 特徴, identifying whose characteristic is being discussed.

3.4.n: Introduces what distinguishes the company from others.

3.5.n: Combines with は to frame the following statement as a company characteristic.

3.6.n: Marks the company’s defining feature as the topic.

3.8.n: Modifies 組織 to specify the team’s function.

3.9.n: Refers here to the company’s sales team or structure.

3.10.n: Links 営業組織 to もの, presenting the sales organization as the thing under discussion.

3.11.n: A general noun in というもの that refers back to the sales organization.

3.12.n: Marks the sales organization as what the company forms.

3.13.n: Names the people who make up the sales organization.

3.14.n: Restricts membership to students; it is a more formal alternative to だけ.

3.15.n: Marks students alone as the people used to form the organization.

3.16.n: 形成する becomes 形成している, describing the organization’s established makeup.

3.17.n: Refers to an aspect of the company, not a physical place.

4.0.n: Points back to the sales organization consisting entirely of students.

4.1.n: Marks that previously mentioned aspect as the subject of the judgment.

4.2.n: Before の特徴, ranks this characteristic above the others.

4.3.n: Connects 一番 to 特徴 to express the company’s foremost characteristic.

4.4.n: Names the distinctive quality the speaker considers most important.

4.5.n: Combines with な to add a gently questioning tone to the judgment.

4.6.n: Completes かな, softening the statement rather than asking the listener a direct question.

4.7.n: Marks the preceding judgment as the content of 思います.

4.8.n: The polite form of 思う, presenting the judgment as the speaker’s opinion.

0.lit: I am called Kumagai Manato of Venture House Co., Ltd. I ask for your goodwill.
0.tip: と申します is a humble, polite way to give your name.

1.lit: Currently, we are doing the activity called sales representation as our main focus.
1.tip: やっております is a humble, polite version of やっています.

2.lit: As for products handled, we are permitted to sell telecommunications and electricity-related business offerings, mainly through door-to-door sales.
2.tip: させていただいています often adds business politeness rather than emphasizing actual permission.

3.lit: As a feature of our company, the fact that we have formed the sales organization with students only.
3.tip: ところ means the aspect or fact being highlighted here, not a physical location.

4.lit: That aspect, I think, is perhaps the number-one feature.
4.tip: かなと思います softens an opinion, making it sound less categorical.
